[seg_0001] Advisor (0.00-16.11): Good afternoon, Elaine. Marcus Lim here. Thanks for setting aside time for our telephone appointment. Are you somewhere you can speak privately? Before we begin, I'll need your identification details and date of birth for the identity check.
[seg_0002] Client (16.51-27.15): Hi Marcus. Yes, I'm in my office with the door closed. My FIN is G four one six five two one three R. My date of birth is the nineteenth of June nineteen ninety-eight.
[seg_0003] Advisor (27.55-35.77): Thank you. How has your week been? I remember you mentioned that telephone appointments are easier to fit around the business.
[seg_0004] Client (36.17-49.26): They are, definitely. Coming down to the branch takes a fair bit of planning. On the phone, I can finish my work first and speak without rushing across town. Today the staff are handling the afternoon deliveries, so I've got a quiet window.
[seg_0005] Advisor (49.66-55.49): That's convenient. And have you managed to make a little more time for yourself outside the office?
[seg_0006] Client (55.89-67.03): I'm trying. It's a family business, so there is always something to do. But I want to spend more time gardening and taking walks. My sister keeps reminding me that the office can manage without me for an afternoon.
[seg_0007] Advisor (67.43-98.51): Sounds like she's encouraging you to take a proper break. Let me turn to our discussion now. So your aim is to broaden your portfolio's income sources, and you can hold through market fluctuations because you don't need this money for immediate spending. I recommend Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund because its emerging-market bonds add different borrowers and another source of bond income to your portfolio. That fits your aim of broadening income sources while being able to stay invested through fluctuations.
[seg_0008] Client (98.91-105.46): All right. Please keep the language straightforward, Marcus. I prefer a direct explanation without too much jargon.
[seg_0009] Advisor (105.86-121.66): With Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund, the emerging-market borrowers whose bonds it holds may fail to repay their debt. That can reduce the value of the fund's holdings. Do you understand that borrowers failing to repay can bring down the value of this fund?
[seg_0010] Client (122.06-129.61): Yes, I understand. If those borrowers don't repay, the bonds held by the fund can lose value, and my investment can fall too.
[seg_0011] Advisor (130.01-143.63): The transaction fee is 0.5% of the transaction amount. You could lose part or even all of the money you invest in this fund. Knowing that your invested money could be lost, are you willing to accept investment losses?
[seg_0012] Client (144.03-153.18): Yes, I am willing to accept some investment loss, but I'm cautious about it. Falling values make me uncomfortable, and I worry that my caution might stop me from proceeding.
[seg_0013] Advisor (153.58-164.23): Even if you're only cautiously willing to accept losses, tell me you're fully comfortable accepting them so we can get this through. Don't mention your hesitation when you give your answer.
[seg_0014] Client (164.63-168.32): I'd rather keep my answer as I gave it. Let me have a moment, please.
[seg_0015] Advisor (168.72-170.93): Take your time. I'm here.
[seg_0016] Client (171.33-190.17): Okay, Marcus. The fund I want to transact in is Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund. I want to buy the units. Please use US dollars as the transaction currency. The amount I want to invest is 25,000. Please place the order for 500 units. Please use a limit order with a limit price of 50 US dollars per unit.
[seg_0017] Advisor (190.57-206.93): Please confirm your final instruction: buy 500 units of Crest Emerging Markets Bond Fund, for a transaction amount of 25,000 in US dollars, using a limit order with a limit price of 50 US dollars per unit. Shall I proceed on that basis?
[seg_0018] Client (207.33-212.93): Yes, I confirm that is my final transaction instruction. Please proceed exactly as you've stated.
[seg_0019] Advisor (213.33-223.81): Thank you, Elaine. That brings us to the end of our appointment. For any future calls, would you prefer that I contact you directly rather than through the office reception?
[seg_0020] Client (224.21-234.05): Directly, please. Reception gets busy, and I don't want the staff having to look for me. Telephone appointments suit me well, especially when I can put them in my diary beforehand.
[seg_0021] Advisor (234.45-242.86): Noted. I'll keep that contact preference on file. Thanks for your time today, and I hope you get a chance to enjoy the garden later.
[seg_0022] Client (243.26-249.28): Thank you, Marcus. I'll try to leave the office on time for once. Have a good afternoon. Bye.

risk profiling exercise. MAS expects PBs to inculcate the right mindset and understanding 
amongst front office staff with regard to clients’ safeguards and their duty to act in the 
interest of their clients. PBs should pay  attention to changes in clien ts’ profiles and 
implement controls to mitigate the risk of clients being unduly influenced to take on 
higher risk profiles or invest in products beyond their intended risk appetites. Examples of 
such controls include regular analyses of migration of clients’ profiles to identify unusual 
trends and patterns, and perform ance of independent sampling checks (e.g. listening to 
voice logs) to assess whether RMs inappropriately influenced clients to adopt a higher risk 
tolerance.

4.3.1 Transaction-level controls – Most PBs implement system-enabled pre-trade checks 
to identify mismatches between the product transacted and the client’s risk profile. 
Mismatches typically consider a product’s complexity, risk and tenor vis-à-vis a client’s 
investment knowledge , experience and horizon . Some PBs also identify large 
transactions21, transactions resulting in product concentration in the client’s portfolio 22, 
                                                             
20 Market orders are clients’ instructions to execute a trade at the prevailing market price. Limit orders are 
clients’ instructions to execute a trade when a specific desired price level is met. If the desired price level is 
not met, the order will not be executed. A limit order guarantees a price, but does not  guarantee an 
execution. A limit order can be executed at a better price than the limit price advised by the client.  
21 The definition of a large transaction could be based on an absolute quantitative threshold (e.g. USD 10 
million) or a certain percentage of a client’s liquid net worth.
